registers.name: CTRL
registers.description: Control register for request launch, fault clearing, and safe mode selection. Write-only control bits pulse internally on write; reads return the current latched software-visible control state.

fields.name: start_request
fields.description: Write 1 to launch a new request. The RTL captures the current request/configuration fields and attempts to issue one bounded outstanding request.

fields.name: clear_faults
fields.description: Write 1 to request clearing of latched faults under supervisory policy.

fields.name: safe_mode_select
fields.description: Firmware-selected safety inhibit/override mode. This does not create a substitute or fallback command.

registers.name: REQUEST
registers.description: Request metadata register containing the compact request sequencing and mode fields.

fields.name: request_seq
fields.description: Firmware-provided sequence identifier for matching request and response lifecycle.

fields.name: flow_condition_sel
fields.description: Flow condition selector used in request packaging and safety validation.

fields.name: control_mode
fields.description: Control mode selector used in request packaging and command policy.

registers.name: REQUEST_VELOCITY
registers.description: Stream velocity register used in request packaging.

fields.name: stream_velocity
fields.description: 32-bit integer or fixed-point stream velocity parameter.

registers.name: GEOMETRY
registers.description: Geometry identifier or handle used in request packaging.

fields.name: geometry_id
fields.description: Geometry identifier or handle.

registers.name: TIMEOUT_CYCLES
registers.description: Programmable timeout deadline in control cycles.

fields.name: timeout_cycles
fields.description: Maximum number of clk cycles allowed before timeout is declared for the outstanding request.

registers.name: FRESHNESS_CYCLES
registers.description: Programmable freshness window in control cycles.

fields.name: freshness_cycles
fields.description: Maximum age window for accepting a response as fresh.

registers.name: ACTUATOR_MIN
registers.description: Lower clamp bound for actuator command generation.

fields.name: actuator_min
fields.description: Minimum allowable actuator command value.

registers.name: ACTUATOR_MAX
registers.description: Upper clamp bound for actuator command generation.

fields.name: actuator_max
fields.description: Maximum allowable actuator command value.

fields.name: rate_limit
fields.description: Optional command rate limit. A value of zero may disable rate limiting by implementation policy.

registers.name: STATUS
registers.description: Primary status register exposing live supervision and fault state.

fields.name: busy
fields.description: One outstanding request is active.

fields.name: response_valid
fields.description: A response has been accepted and is visible to the command path.

fields.name: timeout_fault
fields.description: Timeout fault latched by watchdog supervision.

fields.name: stale_fault
fields.description: Stale response fault latched by response validation.

fields.name: response_seq_mismatch
fields.description: Sequence mismatch fault latched by response validation.

fields.name: invalid_payload_fault
fields.description: Invalid payload fault latched by response validation or safety checks.

fields.name: fallback_active
fields.description: Safety inhibition is active; actuator output validity is deasserted.

fields.name: fault_pending
fields.description: Latched fault pending for firmware handling.

fields.name: current_sequence
fields.description: Current outstanding sequence number.

fields.name: last_good_command
fields.description: Upper half of the command/status mirror. Full last-good-command visibility is provided by LAST_GOOD_COMMAND at 0x2C.

fields.name: last_good_command
fields.description: Last accepted actuator command value.

sources.name: FAULT_IRQ
sources.description: Interrupt asserted according to CSR policy when a latched fault or fault-pending condition requires firmware attention.

sources.name: COMPLETION_IRQ
sources.description: Interrupt asserted according to CSR policy on request completion or response acceptance when enabled by firmware policy.

init_sequence: Program TIMEOUT_CYCLES and FRESHNESS_CYCLES with application-appropriate deadlines.
Program ACTUATOR_MIN, ACTUATOR_MAX, and RATE_LIMIT as needed.
Optionally program REQUEST metadata fields (request_seq, flow_condition_sel, control_mode, geometry_id, stream_velocity) before launching.
Write CTRL.start_request=1 to issue a request; the hardware captures the current request fields and asserts the external request stream valid until ready is observed.
polling_sequence: Poll STATUS.busy until it clears or a fault is observed.
Poll STATUS.response_valid and SEQUENCE.current_sequence for completion correlation.
Poll STATUS.timeout_fault, STATUS.stale_fault, STATUS.response_seq_mismatch, STATUS.invalid_payload_fault, and STATUS.fault_pending for error handling.
Read LAST_GOOD_COMMAND when STATUS.response_valid is set and output validity is permitted by policy.
irq_sequence: On interrupt, read STATUS and SEQUENCE to determine whether the interrupt was caused by completion or fault.
If a fault is present, log the status bits and take software recovery action.
If completion is indicated, read LAST_GOOD_COMMAND and proceed with downstream handling.

consistency_notes: All register offsets are byte-addressed and reachable through the declared Wishbone CSR/MMIO decode.
The register map is compatible with the DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON register_contract and does not invent inaccessible software-visible state.
No substitute or fallback actuator command is defined; on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, actuator output validity is deasserted and faults remain software-visible.
The top-level transport remains firmware-mediated through CSR/MMIO plus bounded valid/ready request and response streams.
The map uses 32-bit accesses because the declared top-level control plane is Wishbone 32-bit, and wider values are not required for any individual access.
